title: Corneal Endothelial Cell Loss after Ciliary Sulcus Placement of Ahmed Glaucoma Valve in Patients with Noninfectious Uveitic Glaucoma

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license)

indication: Glaucoma secondary to noninfectious uveitis (chronic iridocyclitis 10, retinal vasculitis 5, sarcoidosis 4, multifocal choroiditis 3, VKH 3, Fuchs iridocyclitis 1, sympathetic ophthalmia 1); bilateral uveitis 21, unilateral 6; previous cataract surgery 24, trabeculectomy 9, vitrectomy 7 of 27 eyes; 3 eyes with concomitant cataract surgery

groups.description: Ahmed glaucoma valve (FP7) with the tube inserted into the ciliary sulcus through a scleral tunnel, scleral patch graft; single surgeon; inflammation quiescent at surgery

series.baseline_label: Baseline = preoperative central CECD of the operated eye (Topcon SP-3000, technician-verified cell margins)
series.notes: mean ± SD; per-visit n from column N (C2) of Table 2

exclusions.reason: percent change derived from the same series; p-values are not admissible

exclusions.what: jpm-12-02075-t004 unilateral and bilateral uveitis subgroups
exclusions.reason: header sizes (6 + 25) do not add up to the 27-eye cohort (Table 1: 21 bilateral, 6 unilateral), the subgroups are the same eyes as the Table 2 series, and they report only 6 and 12 months; the whole-cohort series is used

exclusions.what: Contralateral eyes of patients with bilateral uveitis (text only)

notes: Retrospective study (2017-2021), one eye per patient (the first-operated eye when both had an AGV); inclusion required a minimum preoperative CECD and more than 12 months of follow-up.
Per-visit n varies (column N), so the means at 3 and 9 months come from a subset of the 27 eyes.
Tube-shunt surgery without an investigational arm; the single cohort is control.
